# Notices and their causes

Every refusal or hold that Clouseau shows on a pull request, in a check summary or in a workflow log carries three things:

1. a **cause class**, a fixed machine-stable name such as `receipt_engine` (the same text is used in the comment, the workflow annotation and this page);
2. one sentence that says what is wrong, with the concrete values that are safe to show: a short commit id, the engine revision, the base that moved, the rule that held, or a file of the pull request itself;
3. **numbered next steps** the customer can run, with exact commands where one exists.

A notice never contains a secret, the contents of a receipt, or a provider's response. A cause class is a key of a closed table in the source (`src/receipt-rejection.cjs`, `src/incomplete.cjs`, `src/gate-notice.cjs`, `src/merge-protection.cjs`, `src/branch-update.cjs`, `src/branch-conflict.cjs`); text from a run is never promoted to a class. `src/notice-causes.test.cjs` fails when a class is added without a sentence, a numbered step and a row on this page.

Commands in steps use `clouseau`, the global launcher of the shared agent installation (`bash scripts/install-agent`), and the GitHub CLI `gh`. `BASE_BRANCH`, `PR_NUMBER`, `REQUIREMENT_FILE` and `RECEIPT_FILE` are placeholders for values only you know.

## Local review receipt not used

A receipt named by the `clouseau-local-review:` marker in the pull request description is either verified in every respect or ignored. An ignored receipt approves nothing. What the run does next depends on the repository:

| Mode | What the notice says |
| --- | --- |
| Local review is required | Nothing is approved until you publish a valid receipt. Shown as an incomplete-review comment with cause `local_receipt_required`. |
| Receipt-only route (a marker is present, no provider key) | This run did not review the change itself. Publish a valid receipt, or remove the marker so the CI AI reviewer runs. Cause `local_receipt_unusable`. |
| Anything else | CI reviewed the change itself; no action is needed. A paragraph at the end of the review comment names the cause. |

The notice reads `Local review receipt not used (cause: \`receipt_<class>\`): <sentence>`, and the incomplete-review comment shows it as `**Cause:** \`local_receipt_required\` (\`receipt_<class>\`)`.

| Cause class | Meaning | First class-specific step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `receipt_absent` | The pull request description carries no `clouseau-local-review:` marker. | Reissue the receipt (below). |
| `receipt_unread` | This hosted run does not read receipts: it follows a receipt-only run, and that run already rejected the receipt (its notice names the cause). | Reissue the receipt (below). |
| `receipt_malformed` | The marker or the published receipt is malformed or unsupported (for example more than one marker, an installation-only receipt, or an artifact that is not a Clouseau receipt). | Reissue the receipt (below). |
| `receipt_unavailable` | The receipt could not be read from the immutable commit the marker names. | Check that the commit named by the marker still exists in this repository and has not been deleted; if it is gone, reissue the receipt. |
| `receipt_signature` | Its signature is not from an enrolled, active key. | Sign with an enrolled identity (`clouseau public-identity` prints the one on this machine); if it is not enrolled or was revoked, ask a repository owner to change the protected `local_review` section of `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch to enroll it. |
| `receipt_author` | Its signer is not enrolled for the author of this pull request. | Sign with an identity enrolled for the pull request author, or ask a repository owner to change the protected `local_review` section of `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch to enroll yours for this author. |
| `receipt_attestation` | It is not a maintainer attestation that the protected configuration permits for this pull request and author. | Have the pull request author run the review, or ask a repository owner to change the protected `local_review` section of `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch to allow `local_review.attest` for this author. |
| `receipt_expired` | It is expired or not yet valid. | Receipts are valid only for a limited time after they are issued; renew this one in the pull request checkout with `clouseau refresh --pr PR_NUMBER --agent claude\|codex\|opencode` (outside an AI harness use `--harness codex\|claude`), which reviews the unchanged head again, reusing the earlier answers, and replaces the marker without pushing the branch, or do the steps below by hand. |
| `receipt_revision_repository` | It was issued for a different repository. | Run the review in a checkout of this repository, not a fork or another project. |
| `receipt_revision_head` | It reviewed an earlier head but this pull request is now at another head. | Any push after a review needs a new review: make your last change first, then review and publish that head. |
| `receipt_revision_base` | It was issued against an earlier base but the base branch is now at a newer commit. | Update the branch with the base: `gh pr update-branch PR_NUMBER` (or `git fetch origin && git merge origin/BASE_BRANCH`; never rebase), then `git pull` if GitHub did it. |
| `receipt_changed` | The protected policy or configuration changed after the receipt was issued. | Merge the current base into the branch (`git fetch origin && git merge origin/BASE_BRANCH`; never rebase) so the review uses the current rules. |
| `receipt_source` | The reviewed sources or diff differ from the pull request. | The review reads committed files only: commit all changes, do not amend or add commits after the review, and make sure the pull request contains exactly the reviewed commits. |
| `receipt_record` | Its review record is incomplete or inconsistent with what was signed. | Do not edit a receipt by hand; discard it and run a fresh review. |
| `receipt_engine` | It was issued by an older Clouseau engine and this run uses the current protected engine, which does not list that engine as review-compatible. | Run the review again: the `clouseau` launcher refreshes to the current protected engine before it starts (pass `--engine latest` to leave a review that was started on an older engine). |
| `receipt_not_passing` | The review it records did not pass. | Open the findings of the local review, repair the blockers within the accepted requirement, and review the new head. |
| `receipt_settings` | The protected chunked review configuration is invalid, so no receipt can be checked. | This is not fixable from the pull request: ask a repository owner to change the protected `local_review` section of `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch (the `chunked` settings), then re-run this check. |
| `receipt_untested` | No supplied test imports changed production code. An empty file (no nonblank line, such as an empty package `__init__.py`) holds no code and is never named. | Add or extend a test that imports each named production file (or the module that wraps it), commit it, and review again. A Rust file is tested by a change inside its own `#[cfg(test)]` test module (with `#[test]` functions) or by a `tests/` integration test that `use`s its module path; production lines changed beside an untouched test module are held, so add or extend a test in that module. |
| `receipt_integrity` | Test integrity is unresolved. | Make the tests prove the change (real assertions on the changed behavior, no weakened or deleted checks), commit, and review again. |
| `receipt_completeness` | Review completeness is unresolved. | Supply the evidence the reviewer could not read (sources or tests it names as missing), commit, and review again. |

Unless the class is `receipt_settings` (a protected configuration the owner must correct), the steps end with the same three that issue a fresh receipt for the current head by hand (`clouseau refresh --pr PR_NUMBER` does them for you; see [Refreshing a pull request](local-review.md#refreshing-a-pull-request-after-its-base-moved)):

1. Commit everything, then review this exact head: `clouseau review --directory . --base origin/BASE_BRANCH --request-file REQUIREMENT_FILE --agent claude|codex|opencode` (outside an AI harness use `--harness codex|claude` instead of `--agent`).
2. Publish the receipt: `clouseau publish --directory . --receipt RECEIPT_FILE`.
3. Put the marker it prints in the pull request description, replacing the old `clouseau-local-review:` marker (editing the description re-runs this check).

Values shown in a sentence are re-validated when rendered: commit ids must be 40 hexadecimal characters (shown as 12), an expiry must be an ISO instant, a branch name must be a plain name, and a file name comes from the pull request's own changed files with markup removed.

## Review incomplete

`Clouseau review incomplete` means no decision could be reached. The comment shows the cause class, one reason sentence and numbered steps. `{repo}` and `{run}` in a step are filled from the workflow run link.

| Cause class | First step |
| --- | --- |
| `provider_key_missing` | Add the provider key repository secret named in the reason: `gh secret set {secret} --repo {repo}`. |
| `provider_key_invalid` | Store the bare key (no spaces, quotation marks or line break) as the repository secret: `gh secret set {secret} --repo {repo}`. |
| `provider_rejected` | The provider refused the credential (HTTP 401 or 403). Create or activate a valid key in the provider console. |
| `provider_payment_required` | The provider refused the request for payment reasons (HTTP 402); the key itself was accepted. Add credit or fix billing on the provider account that owns the key. |
| `provider_unavailable` | No change to this pull request or its secrets is needed: the provider did not answer successfully. Check the provider status page. |
| `local_receipt_required` | Run the local Clouseau review on this exact head: `clouseau review --directory . --base origin/BASE_BRANCH --request-file REQUIREMENT_FILE --agent claude\|codex\|opencode`. |
| `local_receipt_unusable` | Run the local Clouseau review on this exact head and update the receipt marker in the pull request description (`clouseau review ...`, then `clouseau publish --directory . --receipt RECEIPT_FILE`). |
| `review_output_invalid` | The reviewer model answered in an invalid form on every bounded attempt. Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `provider_incomplete` | The reviewer model did not finish its answer within the bounded budget. Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `evidence_budget` | Split the change so that the changed files together fit the 900 KB review evidence budget. |
| `changed_file_unreadable` | Split the file named in the reason out of this change, or make it complete text of at most 300 KB. |
| `lockfile_unsummarizable` | Regenerate the lockfile named in the reason with a supported lockfile version, or split it out of this change. |
| `changed_files_incomplete` | GitHub did not return a patch for every changed file (a very large, binary or truncated diff). Reduce the change so every file has a patch. |
| `tree_truncated` | The repository tree is too large to locate existing tests. Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `investigation_exhausted` | The reviewer could not complete its bounded source investigation. Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `verification_failed` | Open the failing job linked in the reason (when it names one) and fix the failing step. |
| `github_api_error` | GitHub rejected an API request this review needs; the status and endpoint are in the reason. Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `github_rate_limit` | No change is needed: the repository installation token used its GitHub API budget. |
| `receipt_protected_controls` | A local receipt cannot stand in for the owner. Ask a maintainer to comment exactly `/approve-intent {head}` on this pull request. |
| `receipt_history_changed` | The findings on the pull request changed after the receipt was issued. Run the local review again on this exact head so the receipt reflects them (`clouseau review ...`). |
| `chunked_record_invalid` | The signed chunked review record is not consistent with the evidence and protected parameters named in the reason. Run the local Clouseau review again on this exact head (`clouseau review ...`). |
| `decision_mismatch` | The assessment and the stored record disagree (both decisions are in the reason). Re-run only the failed jobs: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `evidence_incomplete` | Open the log of the failed assessment job in the workflow run below for the diagnostic and repair the missing evidence. |

A provider that refuses a request is told apart by its status: 401 or 403 is `provider_rejected` (the credential), 402 is `provider_payment_required` (the account cannot pay; the key itself is valid), anything else is `provider_unavailable`. A credential that is malformed is named before any request is made (`provider_key_missing`, `provider_key_invalid`) with the secret's name and a fixed problem class, never its value.

## Review pending

`Clouseau review pending` is shown while PR verification (tests, exact coverage and package build) has not finished. Nothing is approved. The cause class records the observed state.

| Cause class | What the customer does |
| --- | --- |
| `verification_pending_absent` | No PR verification run exists for this revision. Check that the verification workflow is enabled for this repository (the Actions tab). A pull request opened before that workflow was installed has no run: update the branch so one starts: `gh pr update-branch {number}`. |
| `verification_pending_queued` | Verification is queued for a runner; nothing is needed. The review runs again automatically when verification completes. |
| `verification_pending_running` | Verification is running; nothing is needed. The review runs again automatically when verification completes. |
| `verification_pending_finalizing` | Verification just finished and its results are being recorded; nothing is needed. The review runs again automatically. |
| `verification_pending_unknown` | Verification has not reported a final state; nothing is needed. The review runs again automatically when verification completes. |

## Branch update needed

Cause class `base_moved`. The base branch moved after the revision was assessed, so the assessment, any receipt and the exact-head approval are bound to the old base. The comment names both short commit ids and numbers three steps: `gh pr update-branch PR_NUMBER` (or merge the base; never rebase), wait for the automatic re-review, and, only where a receipt is required, review and publish again on the new head.

## Merge conflict with the base

Cause class `branch_conflict`. GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows for a pull request that has a merge conflict with its base, so PR verification (tests, exact coverage and package build) never exists for the revision and the pull request would otherwise show nothing. The `pull_request_target` run still starts; while it waits for a verification run that is absent, it reads the pull request's mergeability from GitHub. Only a definite `mergeable: false` in state `dirty` on the assessed head is a conflict: a value still being computed (`mergeable: null`) is re-read up to four times, with waits of 2, 4 and 8 seconds, and if it is still unknown nothing is posted and the ordinary wait continues. A conflict ends the wait at once instead of after the queue grace and replaces the generic pending notice with one comment, `Clouseau: merge conflict`, bound by a hidden marker to the head and the base commit: a rerun posts nothing, a base that moves again updates the same comment, and a new head gets its own. The comment names the base branch (GitHub does not expose which files conflict; the merge in step 1 lists them) and numbers three steps: merge the base and resolve (`git fetch origin && git merge origin/BASE_BRANCH`; never rebase), refresh the review evidence and push once (`clouseau refresh --pr PR_NUMBER ...`, or review, publish, update the marker and push by hand), and wait: verification starts only after the conflict is resolved and pushed.

## Merge not armed (repository settings)

Cause class `merge_protection_insufficient`. Clouseau recorded its decision and approval but did not arm the merge. The comment lists each bounded gap with the change that closes it, then asks for a re-run.

| Gap | Step |
| --- | --- |
| auto-merge disabled | Enable auto-merge: `gh repo edit {repo} --enable-auto-merge`. |
| main not protected | Protect the base branch with a ruleset or branch protection (Settings, Rules); `gh api repos/{repo}/rulesets` lists existing rulesets. |
| required checks missing | Add the Clouseau verification and policy jobs as required status checks of the base branch ruleset. |
| up-to-date missing | Turn on "Require branches to be up to date before merging" in the base branch ruleset. |
| approval freshness missing | In the ruleset require one approving review, dismiss stale approvals on push, and require approval of the most recent push. |
| force-push+deletion protection missing | Add the "Restrict deletions" and "Block force pushes" rules to the base branch ruleset. |

## Maintainer request

When a maintainer's second opinion is required, the comment and the check summary carry the `/approve-intent` command and one of these cause classes.

| Cause class | First step |
| --- | --- |
| `intent_bot_authored` | A maintainer submits an approving review of this exact revision, because the approval bot cannot approve its own pull request: `gh pr review {number} --approve --repo {repo}`. |
| `intent_protected_controls` | Review the protected-control change (the sentence above names the rule), then have a maintainer confirm it. |
| `intent_incomplete_patch` | Reduce the change so GitHub returns a patch for every file, or review the withheld files by hand. |
| `intent_owner_decision` | Read the review above; if it is correct, have a maintainer confirm the change belongs in this repository. |

## Gate stopped

When the approval gate stops, its check summary shows the gate's own sentence followed by one of these classes. An error that is not in the table is `gate_failed`.

| Cause class | First step |
| --- | --- |
| `gate_verification_failed` | Open the failing job linked above and fix the failing step. |
| `auto_merge_not_armed` | Allow auto-merge for the repository: `gh repo edit {repo} --enable-auto-merge`. |
| `auto_merge_must_be_off` | Turn auto-merge off for this pull request: `gh pr merge {number} --disable-auto --repo {repo}`. |
| `assessment_pending` | Wait for the AI assessment to finish after verification; the gate runs again with its result. |
| `intent_required` | A maintainer comments exactly `/approve-intent {head}` on this pull request. This confirms intent only; all tests and coverage remain mandatory. |
| `revision_changed` | A push or a base change happened while the gate ran, so its result belongs to an older revision. |
| `verification_not_finished` | If this pull request comes from a fork, a maintainer approves its workflow runs (Actions tab, "Approve and run"). |
| `confirmation_withdrawn` | A maintainer comments exactly `/approve-intent {head}` on this pull request. This confirms intent only; all tests and coverage remain mandatory. |
| `ownership_changed` | Code ownership changed while the gate ran. Re-run the failed job: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `code_owner_approval_required` | A code owner approves the current head of this pull request: `gh pr review {number} --approve --repo {repo}`. |
| `protection_mode_changed` | The repository protection settings changed while the gate ran. Re-run the failed job: `gh run rerun {run} --failed --repo {repo}`. |
| `gate_failed` | Open the failed job log of the workflow run for the full error. |

## Local review notices

`clouseau review` prints these to stderr and lists their cause classes under `notices` in its result.

| Cause class | Meaning | Steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verification_tool_missing` | A verification command needs a program or module that is not installed (a program that cannot start, `No module named X`, or `X: not found`). The program name is shown only when it is a plain name. | Install it (for `coverage`: `python3 -m pip install -r requirements-test.txt`; for `c8`: `npm ci`; otherwise put it on PATH), then run the review again on the same commit. |
| `verification_tool_shadowed` | A verification command ran `python -m X` and a directory named `X` in the directory it runs from was found before the installed module (Python: `'X' is a package and cannot be directly executed`), typically a leftover `coverage/` report directory. The module name is shown only when it is a plain name. | Move or delete that directory; if the failure remains, install the module in the Python on PATH (for `coverage`: `python3 -m pip install -r requirements-test.txt`, or put a virtualenv that has it first on PATH), then run the review again on the same commit. |
| `local_recipe_edited` | The change edits `.clouseau-local.json`, so local review verified the recipe from the base branch, not the edit (a change cannot weaken its own checks). | Land a wanted edit in its own pull request first and review this change on the new base, or revert the edit. |

## Declared coverage

The `declared` coverage mode ([declared coverage](declared-coverage.md)) fails the coverage step with one of these classes. The step prints `Declared coverage (cause: <class>): <sentence>` followed by numbered steps. For a multi-artifact plan the header names the part and its declaration file: `Declared coverage (cause: <class>) for coverage part N (<format>, source <source>, declaration <dir>/package.json): <sentence>`, and every failing part is reported under its own class; the approval gate then reports `gate_verification_failed` for the failed job.

| Cause class | Meaning | First step |

# Notices and their causes

Every refusal or hold that Clouseau shows on a pull request, in a check summary or in a workflow log carries three things:

1. a **cause class**, a fixed machine-stable name such as `receipt_engine` (the same text is used in the comment, the workflow annotation and this page);
2. one sentence that says what is wrong, with the concrete values that are safe to show: a short commit id, the engine revision, the base that moved, the rule that held, or a file of the pull request itself;
3. **numbered next steps** the customer can run, with exact commands where one exists.

A notice never contains a secret, the contents of a receipt, or a provider's response. A cause class is a key of a closed table in the source (`src/receipt-rejection.cjs`, `src/incomplete.cjs`, `src/gate-notice.cjs`, `src/merge-protection.cjs`, `src/branch-update.cjs`, `src/branch-conflict.cjs`); text from a run is never promoted to a class. `src/notice-causes.test.cjs` fails when a class is added without a sentence, a numbered step and a row on this page.

Commands in steps use `clouseau`, the global launcher of the shared agent installation (`bash scripts/install-agent`), and the GitHub CLI `gh`. `BASE_BRANCH`, `PR_NUMBER`, `REQUIREMENT_FILE` and `RECEIPT_FILE` are placeholders for values only you know.

# Receipt compatibility across engine revisions

A signed local review receipt names the engine revision that produced it (`reviewer_sha`, `reviewer_digest`). Today CI
accepts it only when that is exactly the protected `main` it resolved. `main` moves many times a day, so a receipt
rots within hours and CI repeats a review (about $6 and several minutes) even when the engine change cannot affect what
the review attests. This design lets CI accept a receipt issued under revision X while running revision Y, if and only if
Y itself declares X's review semantics compatible. If CI cannot establish that, it behaves as it does today: the receipt is
ignored and CI reviews.

## Design

**Review-semantics digest.** `src/review-semantics.cjs` hashes every engine file under the same roots as the exact engine
digest (`action.yml`, `src`, `policy`, `bin`, `skills`, `scripts`; tests excluded) *except* the files listed in its
`NEUTRAL` table. Each neutral file has a written reason. A file is semantic by default: a new or renamed file is part of
the meaning until a person lists it as neutral. The table lives in `review-semantics.cjs`, which is itself semantic, so
moving a file into it changes the digest and forces the same decision as editing the file would.

**Compatibility statement.** `policy/review-compatibility.json` is in-tree on protected main:

```json
{"version": 1, "current": "<digest of this tree>", "compatible": ["<older digest>", "..."]}
```

`current` must equal the digest of the tree that contains it. `compatible` lists earlier semantics whose receipts this
tree accepts (at most 64, newest first, never including `current`). The statement is the only source of compatibility.

Two further files exist only to keep the statement in step with the tree, and `acceptor()` never reads them:

- `compat/manifest.json` lists the semantic files (path, executable bits, content hash) the statement was last folded for.
  Its digest must equal `current`. It lets a tool say which semantic files changed since the fold by comparing two file
  lists, with no Git history.
- `compat/declarations/<digest>.json`, one file per pull request, state that a set of semantic files changed (by content
  hash, or deleted) and whether the change is `compatible` or `incompatible`. A declaration is inert until it is folded.

**Receipt.** A receipt additionally signs `reviewer_semantics`, the digest of the engine that issued it. Receipts without
the field behave exactly as before.

**Acceptance.** `verifySignedRecord` keeps every check it has (enrolled key, author, expiry, record binding, repository,
head, base, policy and configuration digests, recomputed decision, passing result). Only when the exact engine comparison
fails, and only in central-source mode, it asks `acceptor()` whether the receipt's `reviewer_semantics` is acceptable.
`acceptor()` reads the statement from the engine checkout that is running, the checkout `identifyEngine` and
`verifyEngine` already bound to the SHA the resolver read from protected `gaulatti/clouseau` `main`. It answers yes only
if the statement parses, `current` equals the digest it computes from that checkout, and the claim is `current` or listed.
Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

Declarations chain: after A to B and B to C were both declared compatible, A's receipts are accepted under C. When two pull
requests are folded together, their combined step is compatible only if both declared `compatible`. If a series of small
changes could add up to a different review, declare the last one incompatible. After about 50 further `compatible` folds the
64-entry cap drops the oldest digests and receipts issued under them are ignored again.

Two pull requests that edit the **same** semantic file are the one case that still needs a second declaration: Git may merge
the text, but the merged content then matches neither declaration, so `verify` fails until one author deletes their
declaration and declares again. That is the safe direction.

## Why the list cannot go stale silently (the enforcement argument)

The risk is a semantic change that nobody declared, so that CI accepts a receipt from a weaker or different review. The
argument has four steps.

1. The digest is a function of the bytes of the semantic files, so any semantic change changes it. Reverting restores the
   old digest, which is sound because the bytes are identical.
2. The statement is rejected unless `current` equals the digest of its own tree (`acceptor()`; unchanged by the declare
   and fold flow). The engine's required `verify` job asserts that every semantic file that differs from the manifest is
   covered by exactly one valid declaration, so a change to a semantic file cannot merge without a visible
   `--compatible` or `--incompatible` decision bound to that file's content. Between the merge and the fold, `current`
   no longer equals the digest of the tree, so `acceptor()` answers no to everything: receipts are ignored and CI reviews.
   Only the fold turns a decision into a statement, and it applies the same checks as `verify`.
3. Default-semantic classification closes the "unclassified file" gap: adding a file, renaming one or editing the neutral
   table all change the digest. Listing a file as neutral requires a reason, and the test fails if semantic code loads or
   names any neutral file (apart from `src/cli-usage.cjs`, marked presentation), so a dependency cannot be mislabelled
   neutral by accident.
4. The statement, the manifest, the declarations, the module, the test and every other file under `src/`, `policy/`,
   `compat/`, `scripts/`, `bin/` and `skills/` are protected review controls (`sensitive_paths`). A change to them already needs the owner's exact-revision confirmation.
   The enforcement is a ratchet that makes the owner's compatibility decision unavoidable and visible, not a technical lock
   against an owner who approves a wrong declaration.

There is deliberately a window between a merge and its fold in which main's statement is stale. It is safe because
`acceptor()` refuses everything then (receipts are ignored and CI reviews), and it is short: the fold follows the merge's
review workflow, any push that touches `compat/declarations/`, and a half-hourly schedule. If a fold cannot run or fails,
the window stays open and CI keeps reviewing; nothing is ever accepted on the strength of an unfolded declaration.

## Threat analysis

Attacker: the holder of an enrolled signing key, who is also the PR author, or the PR author alone.

| Attempt | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Receipt claims a `reviewer_semantics` that the running engine does not list | Ignored (`engine`); CI reviews |
| Receipt or PR supplies its own statement or digest | There is no input path: the statement is read only from the resolved protected engine checkout |
| PR edits `policy/review-compatibility.json` in the consumer or engine repository | The consumer's checkout is never read; in the engine repository CI runs the frozen protected main, not the PR |
| PR adds a declaration, or edits the manifest, to hide or reclassify a semantic change | Declarations are inert to `acceptor()`. `verify` binds each to the content hash of the files it names, and a manifest that does not hash to `current` fails; both are protected paths |
| PR changes a semantic file and no declaration covers it | `verify` fails; the PR cannot merge |
| A declaration is run through the fold from a pull request or a fork | The fold runs only on `gaulatti/clouseau` `refs/heads/main`, from a main-only checkout, and refuses elsewhere |
| Weak engine fork signs a receipt naming a real compatible digest | Same trust as today: an enrolled key already vouches for `reviewer_sha`/`reviewer_digest`, which CI cannot re-derive from the receipt. Not widened; see residual risks |
| Receipt from an unlisted or retired semantics, or from a fixed-digest (non central-source) trust | Ignored; fixed-digest trust never uses this path |
| Tampering with `reviewer_semantics` after signing | Breaks the signature |
| Replaying a compatible receipt on another head, base, repository, author, policy or configuration | All existing bindings still apply |
| Statement unreadable, malformed, stale, or the digest cannot be computed (symlink, missing file) | `acceptor()` answers no; receipt ignored |

## Failure modes

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Receipt has no `reviewer_semantics` | Today's behaviour: exact engine match or ignored |
| Old CI engine meets a receipt with the new field | Unknown field: `malformed`, ignored (fail closed) |
| Statement stale after a semantic change | Undeclared: engine test fails. Declared and merged but not yet folded: receipts are ignored until the fold |
| Declarations inconsistent with the tree, or fold cannot push | Fold changes nothing and fails; receipts stay ignored |
| Semantics digest unknown to the statement | Ignored |
| More than 64 digests listed | Statement malformed, receipts ignored |
| Receipt older than 48 hours | Expired by the existing rule, whatever the statement lists |

## Rollout

Consumers change nothing: their workflows already resolve protected main, and the receipt format only gains an optional
signed field. The work lands as independent pull requests that change no behaviour until the last one:

1. Semantics digest, statement, maintainer tool and enforcement test (this document). Nothing calls them.
2. Receipt format: an optional signed `reviewer_semantics`, accepted by the verifier and issued when a caller supplies it,
   and an optional acceptance hook consulted only after an exact engine mismatch. No caller passes either.
3. Integrator: local review supplies the digest when it issues a receipt, and the verifier's hook defaults to
   `acceptor()`. Receipts issued from that point carry the field; receipts of the preceding revisions are not retrofitted
   and stay governed by exact match. To roll back, make the hook default `null` again; no receipt or statement needs to
   change.

Each pull request that changes semantic files declares the change (`declare`); none of them edits the statement.

## Residual risks

- The receipt's engine claim is not independently re-derived. A signer with an enrolled key could claim a compatible
  digest while running modified code. This is the existing trust in the enrolled signer; a later hardening can fetch the
  claimed revision and recompute its semantics digest.
- Chained declarations can hide a cumulative change (see above).
- A wrong `--compatible` is a human error the system makes visible but cannot detect.
- The neutral table is conservative; moving more files into it (with a reason) reduces how often a declaration is needed.
- The fold and the maintainer tool (`src/review-compatibility-cli.cjs`, `scripts/review-compatibility`) are receipt-neutral, as `bump`
  always was, so editing them does not change the digest; they are protected review controls and `src/review-compatibility-cli.test.cjs`
  pins their behaviour. `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml` is pinned by `.github/tests/compat-fold.test.mjs` (permissions, refs, no
  secret, plain push to main).

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

`Clouseau review pending` is shown while PR verification (tests, exact coverage and package build) has not finished. Nothing is approved. The cause class records the observed state.

| --- | --- |

## Skipped verification step without an attesting receipt

When the verification job succeeds with a required step `skipped` (a workflow gated it on `operation: attested`) and the engine,
re-checking the receipt in the trusted workflow, finds that it no longer attests the verification, the verification counts as
failed (a `blocked_technical` decision) with the reason `Required verification step "NAME" concluded skipped`. When a receipt was claimed and refused,
the reason continues with its receipt class and the values that class may show, for example:

> … concluded skipped: the pull request's local review receipt no longer attests the verification (cause: `receipt_expired`: it is expired or not yet valid (it expires `2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`)). Re-run the verification workflow for this head so CI runs the step itself, or renew the receipt first with `clouseau refresh --pr PR_NUMBER` so the step can be skipped again.

Any other class names itself the same way and ends with the one step: re-run the verification workflow for this head, so CI runs
the step itself. Without a marker, or with a valid receipt that attests no verification, the reason is the plain sentence as before.
Nothing from the receipt itself appears in the reason.

## Branch update needed

Cause class `base_moved`. The base branch moved after the revision was assessed, so the assessment, any receipt and the exact-head approval are bound to the old base. # Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
